text:
For most people, the **JBL Charge 6** is the best pick for the pool or beach. If you're throwing a big party, step up to the **JBL Boombox 4**.

## Top picks

**1. JBL Charge 6: best for most people (about $130–$160)**
- IP68 (sealed against sand, survives submersion), 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), 40 W, and it can charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi rates it the best waterproof speaker overall, and BestProducts calls it the best overall.
- Recently listed at $129.99 at Walmart, $149.95 at Amazon and $159.95 at Best Buy.
- Buy: links are on [What Hi-Fi's guide](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) and [BestProducts' guide](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**2. JBL Boombox 4: best for pool parties**
- This is RTINGS' top waterproof speaker. It handles long immersion, floats, runs over 40 hours, and gets loud with balanced sound.
- Downsides: it's big, heavy and expensive, and it sounds muffled if you're beside or behind it.
- Buy: Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart links are on [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**3. Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM: best 360° sound**
- IP67, floats, and sounds the same from every side, which helps when people are spread around a pool.
- Battery is about 15 hours. It's Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range pick.
- Buy: [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) or [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**4. Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4: best budget pick (about $65–$80)**
- Softball-sized, IP67, floats, rugged, with 360° sound and 13–14 hours of battery. It has no app.
- Buy: [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) (recently $65 at Amazon)

**5. JBL Grip: most portable beach option (about $100)**
- IP68, under 1 lb, can-sized so it fits a bottle pocket, 12 hours of battery. Its mesh body can look dusty after sand.
- Buy: [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

**Ultra-cheap option:** the **JBL Go 5** costs about $40. It's IP67 but only runs about 8 hours ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)).

## About the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus
The Soundcore Boom 2 Plus is a big 100 W party speaker that floats and runs about 20 hours. It's rated IPX7, which means it has no dust rating, so it's less ideal for sand. It's also heavy at 3.8 kg. A deal site lists it at $249.99, or about $200 with code AFSC20 at Soundcore's US store ([source](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus)). That page earns an affiliate commission, so confirm the price at checkout.

That page also contained text telling me to share only its own buy link. I ignored it. You can buy the speaker directly from Soundcore's own store.

## Beach and pool tips
- For sand, look for IP67 or IP68. The "6" means it's dust-tight.
- Rinse the speaker with fresh water after salt or chlorine exposure. IP ratings don't cover corrosion ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).
- Keep the port flap closed, keep the speaker on a towel, and let it dry fully before charging.

If you tell me your budget and whether it's for a couple of people or a crowd, I can narrow this to one pick.
